name: CIFAR-10 text→image DiT
summary: Text-conditioned DiT trained with rectified flow on CIFAR-10 32×32 in MLX. Each experiment trains for 120 s; the metric is val_loss (velocity MSE), lower is better.

baseline.label: 2-layer transformer
baseline.detail: Byte tokens (L = 48) → 2 pre-LN transformer blocks → masked mean-pool to one vector.

baseline.label: 4×4 patches · sin-cos pos
baseline.detail: 32×32×3 image → N = 64 tokens of width d = 256, with fixed 2D sin-cos positions.

baseline.label: adaLN-Zero (t + text)
baseline.detail: A timestep MLP plus the projected text vector set each block's LayerNorm shift, scale and gate. Gates start at zero, so every block starts as the identity.

baseline.label: 8 blocks · d256 · 4 heads
baseline.detail: 8 DiT blocks: full self-attention over the 64 patch tokens, then a 4× GELU MLP.

baseline.label: adaLN final layer → velocity
baseline.detail: Zero-initialized linear layer back to 4×4×3 patches. Predicts the velocity v = ε − x.

baseline.label: Rectified flow · t ~ U(0, 1)
baseline.detail: x_t = (1 − t)·x + t·ε, MSE on the velocity. 10% caption dropout trains the unconditional branch for CFG.

baseline.label: AdamW 5e-4 · β(0.9, 0.99) · wd 0
baseline.detail: AdamW with peak learning rate 5e-4, betas (0.9, 0.99), and no weight decay.

baseline.label: 5% warmup · 30% linear warmdown
baseline.detail: Time-based: progress = elapsed / 120 s. Linear warmup over the first 5%, flat, then linear to 0 over the last 30%.

baseline.label: 128 images / step
baseline.detail: 128 CIFAR-10 images and their captions per optimizer step.

baseline.label: Euler · 32 steps · CFG 2.0
baseline.detail: Renders the fixed prompt from 16 fixed seeds after every run. It does not affect val_loss.

1.label: Cosine decay
1.note: Bug: the cosine was inverted, so the LR rose at the end of training.

3.label: Cosine (fixed)
3.note: No-op: a missing math import left the schedule unchanged.

4.label: Weight EMA
4.note: Crashed: lazy arrays grew memory without mx.eval each step, and the EMA state names didn't match the model's.

hypotheses.text: A 2-minute run is step-bound: changes that buy more steps beat changes that add capacity.
adaLN-Zero tolerates a much higher learning rate.
Text-encoder capacity matters little on CIFAR-10 captions.
Warmup is unnecessary at this scale.
Weight decay helps a model trained for 2 minutes.
Faster second-moment adaptation (β2 0.95) helps short runs.
Cosine decay beats linear warmdown. Both attempts had bugs.
An EMA of the weights lowers eval loss.
